header: THE BIG NUMBER CARDS. A short table that holds ONE amount per row (a deposit per size of house, a premium per month, a rate per grade) is the kind of answer a reader's eye goes to first when the amounts stand as large cards. The writer is told not to repeat the table's numbers in a chart, so on some runs it drew the cards and on others it did not (my words, 11 Nov 2026: "that kind of result attracts the users eye ... that is a must where it is possible"). So I build the cards here, from the table's own cells, which the engine has already checked against the circulars: no figure is new. Pure.

symbols.name: MIN_CARDS
doc: how many cards are worth drawing: I take two to four rows, each with its own figure

symbols.name: kpiFromTable
symbols.sig: export function kpiFromTable(t: SynthesisTable | null | undefined): SynthesisChart | null
doc: Returns the cards of one table, or null when it is not that shape: every row has an amount (or a percentage) first in the same column, all in one unit, and the figures are not all alike.

symbols.name: withKpiCards
doc: Returns the result with cards added when it has none and fewer than two charts, taken from the first table that gives them. I never change the result in place.

behaviours: a one-amount-per-row table gives cards, one per row, with the figure as the circular's table gives it
each card keeps its row's label and the cell's own words as the detail
the cards carry the table's title, the column heading and the table's sources
a table of words and multiples is not cards
a table whose amounts are all alike is not cards (nothing to compare)
five rows are a table, not cards
two units in one column are not drawn side by side
a row with no figure first spoils the column
one row is not a comparison
percentages are cards too, in one unit
the first column that fits is used, thousands commas read, rupees without a scale are ₹
the cards are added from the second table when the first gives none
the result is not changed in place
never a second set of cards
